title: Context-aware escalation target for jit-execution-lead
description:
Changes jit-execution-lead's escalation target from a hardcoded human to "whoever invoked it" — the human when run standalone, the parent lead when nested under jit-project-lead — without changing behavior for existing standalone use.

## Background

jit-execution-lead's escalation policy currently always names the human as the target for every escalation case (scope expansion, cross-epic dependency, criteria changes, and others). Once jit-project-lead can dispatch jit-execution-lead as a subagent, an escalation from a nested execution lead should surface to the dispatching lead first, not skip straight to the human.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Every escalation case in jit-execution-lead's escalation policy and matching SKILL.md wording names "the invoker" as the target rather than a hardcoded human.
- [hard] REQ-02: When jit-execution-lead runs standalone (no parent lead invoked it), the invoker defaults to the human and escalation behavior is unchanged from today.
- [hard] REQ-03: When jit-execution-lead runs as a subagent dispatched by a parent lead, escalations surface to that parent lead instead of the human.

## Notes

This is the single change this epic makes to jit-execution-lead; everything else about it is reused unmodified.
